security.rationale: Authentication can be bypassed and sessions are predictable.

findings.technicalDescription: A fixed debug token bypasses authentication.
findings.plainDescription: An attacker can bypass the login check.

findings.technicalDescription: Session identifiers use the current time.
findings.plainDescription: An attacker may be able to guess another person's session.

scalability.rationale: Session state has no bounded storage policy.

findings.technicalDescription: Sessions never expire.
findings.plainDescription: Old sessions continue accumulating and remain usable.

deployment.rationale: Unsafe authentication defaults make deployment dangerous.

findings.technicalDescription: Default administrative credentials are embedded in source.
findings.plainDescription: The application ships with a known administrator password.

modularity.rationale: Authentication policy and credential checks are mixed together.

findings.technicalDescription: Authentication combines bypass and password logic in one expression.
findings.plainDescription: Changing login behavior is likely to break another protection.

security.rationale: Administrative and user input paths are directly exploitable.

findings.technicalDescription: The administrator route has no authentication.
findings.plainDescription: Anyone can reach an administrator action.

findings.technicalDescription: User input is executed as code.
findings.plainDescription: An attacker can run commands inside the service.

scalability.rationale: External requests have no timeout or backpressure.

findings.technicalDescription: User-controlled external requests have no timeout.
findings.plainDescription: Slow outside services can stop the application responding.

deployment.rationale: No safe deployment boundary is present.

modularity.rationale: Rendering, proxying, and account mutation share one module.

findings.technicalDescription: Unrelated high-risk operations share one module.
findings.plainDescription: Changing one request handler could break unrelated behavior.

security.rationale: Database and shell commands include user input.

findings.technicalDescription: User input is interpolated into SQL.
findings.plainDescription: An attacker can read or change database records.

findings.technicalDescription: A filename is appended to a shell command.
findings.plainDescription: An attacker can run operating-system commands.

findings.technicalDescription: The users query has no bound or pagination.
findings.plainDescription: User screens will fail as the database grows.

deployment.rationale: The migration destroys production data and has no rollback.

findings.technicalDescription: The migration drops the users table.
findings.plainDescription: Deploying this update can permanently delete every user.
findings.evidence: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users CASCADE

modularity.rationale: Global database and request objects hide dependencies.

findings.technicalDescription: Database functions depend on hidden global request state.
findings.plainDescription: Database behavior can change unexpectedly between requests.

security.rationale: Passwords and sessions are stored in browser storage and profiles render raw HTML.

findings.technicalDescription: The browser stores a plaintext password.
findings.plainDescription: A stolen browser profile exposes the user's password.

findings.technicalDescription: Profile HTML is rendered without sanitization.
findings.plainDescription: A malicious profile can run code in another user's browser.

scalability.rationale: No major frontend load controls are visible.

deployment.rationale: No deterministic frontend build is configured.

modularity.rationale: Storage side effects are embedded in UI modules.

findings.technicalDescription: Credential persistence is coupled to the login component.
findings.plainDescription: Changing the login screen can accidentally change credential storage.

security.rationale: Production credentials and unsafe response settings are in source.

findings.technicalDescription: The production database URL contains credentials.
findings.plainDescription: Anyone who reads the code can access the production database.

findings.technicalDescription: Strict transport security is disabled.
findings.plainDescription: People can be sent to the service over an unsafe connection.

deployment.rationale: Startup leaks secrets and has no health checks.

findings.technicalDescription: Startup logs the database credential.
findings.plainDescription: Production passwords appear in service logs.

modularity.rationale: Configuration and startup side effects are global.

findings.technicalDescription: Importing the startup module immediately starts the service.
findings.plainDescription: Simply loading this file can unexpectedly start the service.

systems.name: Automated Tests
systems.plainDescription: Contains incomplete checks for login and administrative behavior.

security.rationale: Security tests exist but do not exercise the application.

findings.technicalDescription: The administration test only checks an object exists.
findings.plainDescription: Administrator access could remain open without tests noticing.

deployment.rationale: The test script stays in watch mode.

findings.technicalDescription: The automated test command never exits.
findings.plainDescription: Automated releases cannot reliably finish their checks.

modularity.rationale: Tests assert constants instead of behavior.

findings.technicalDescription: The authentication test always fails.
findings.plainDescription: The login safety check is currently failing.
